items.summary: Renders one stable user/assistant turn and dispatches every normalized message part without owning runtime state.
useWhen: Rendering protocol-neutral chat turns from stable message and part IDs
avoidWhen: Rendering an unstructured text log or inferring lifecycle state from prose
accessibility: Ordered list item with a labelled turn article
Visible terminal status with coarse announcements
examples: Render ChatTurn values projected by an adapter
nonExamples: Pass provider events directly to Turn

items.summary: Renders sanitized streaming Markdown and explicitly disclosed reasoning with terminal state.
useWhen: Displaying model-authored prose or reasoning from a normalized part
avoidWhen: Displaying commands, file paths, or structured tool evidence
accessibility: Preserves heading, list, table, and code semantics
Token deltas are not a live log
examples: Render a TextPart with status=streaming while retaining its complete source
nonExamples: Enable raw HTML or unsafe image URLs in generated Markdown

items.summary: Presents one compact tool lifecycle line with progressively disclosed, lossless evidence.
useWhen: Showing normalized tool input, execution, permission, result, error, or cancellation
avoidWhen: Adding a second spinner or dropping an unknown tool
accessibility: Tool and status remain visible text
examples: Fall through to GenericTool for an unregistered MCP tool
nonExamples: Render every running tool as an inset loading card

items.summary: Specializes coding-agent evidence while preserving the common tool lifecycle contract.
useWhen: A validated ToolPresentation names a supported coding operation
avoidWhen: Tool input does not validate for the specialization; use GenericTool instead
sideEffects: Named callbacks may open a child session or external HTTP(S) source
accessibility: Commands, paths, and coordinates remain LTR
Large outputs use labelled bounded regions
examples: Render normalized file hunks and diagnostics from edit metadata
nonExamples: Parse visible tool labels to recover file or child-session identity

items.summary: Arbitrates consequential requests ahead of the composer while retaining exact origin and decision identity.
useWhen: A session or descendant session has an unresolved permission or question
avoidWhen: Implementing permission policy or network mutations inside presentation
sideEffects: Invokes exact request ID and origin session callbacks supplied by the adapter
accessibility: Moves focus from an active composer to the request heading
Restores focus only when ownership remains in the request
examples: Render a child-session permission with its origin label
nonExamples: Auto-approve a visually similar request or use Escape as rejection

items.summary: Edits a controlled structured draft with native text behavior, typed references, files, commands, and model controls.
useWhen: Composing prompt or shell input against explicit runtime capabilities
avoidWhen: Mutating transport state or interpreting ordinary prose as shell input
sideEffects: Invokes controlled draft, attachment, submit, and stop callbacks
accessibility: Picker, paste, and drop have equivalent button access
examples: Provide capabilities and update ComposerDraft on every edit and semantic selection change
nonExamples: Show an attachment or follow-up control unsupported by the runtime

items.summary: Makes queued work, revert recovery, submission failure, connection loss, and coarse stream state explicit.
useWhen: The adapter exposes recoverable session or submission state
avoidWhen: Showing fake retry or redo controls without a supported callback
accessibility: Routine stream state uses one coarse status region
examples: Restore a reverted prompt only after the user chooses Edit prompt
nonExamples: Clear queued prompts automatically when Stop is invoked
